item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
085
ABPZ20 KNHC 160515
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Oct 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Simon, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane
Trudy, located a few hundred miles southwest of Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression could form during the latter half of next week
while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward over the
eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 160851
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
...MAJOR HURRICANE TRUDY FORECAST TO APPROACH THE SOUTHWESTERN AND
WEST-CENTRAL COAST OF MEXICO THIS WEEKEND...
...TROPICAL STORM WARNING HAS BEEN EXTENDED NORTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.2N 102.4W
ABOUT 250 MI...400 KM SW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 355 MI...570 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...956 MB...28.23 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has extended the Tropical Storm Warning
northward from Punta San Telmo to Manzanillo.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Punta San Telmo to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo southward to Zihuatanejo
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 14.2 North, longitude 102.4 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 6 mph (9 km/h). A north-northwestward to 
northwestward motion at a slightly faster forward speed is forecast 
during the next few days. On the forecast track, the center of Trudy 
will approach the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico on 
Saturday and pass near the coast Saturday night into Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Trudy is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional strengthening is expected through 
Saturday, and Trudy is forecast to remain a major hurricane when it 
makes its closest approach to Mexico. Some weakening is predicted 
later this weekend and into early next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 956 mb (28.23 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the tropical
storm warning area by late tonight or early Saturday. Hurricane
conditions are possible in the hurricane watch area by late
Saturday, with tropical storm conditions beginning on Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 12 inches along and near
the southwest coast of Mexico in Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco.
This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
coast of Mexico in Guerrero. This rainfall may result in localized
flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas along steep
terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern Mexico and will spread northward toward west-central
Mexico during the next few days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 AM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 160852
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
300 AM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Trudy has rapidly strengthened into a major hurricane overnight. Its
15-n-mi wide eye, which is evident in proxy-visible and infrared
satellite imagery, is surrounded by a solid ring of very deep
convection with cloud tops colder than -70 deg C. A prominent outer
band wraps around the northwestern portion of the circulation. The
initial intensity is set at 105 kt for this advisory, trending
closer to recent Dvorak estimates in lieu of the objective estimates
that appear too low given Trudy's impressive satellite structure.
 
The hurricane unexpectedly moved westward for several hours tonight
and now appears to be drifting northward, but using a longer-term
estimate yields a slow northwestward motion (325/5 kt). The track
guidance is clustered on Trudy moving north-northwestward today
before turning back toward the northwest tonight and into the
weekend in response to a building ridge over Mexico. This will bring
the center of Trudy very near the coast of southwestern and
west-central Mexico in 48-60 h. The NHC track forecast shifted
westward this cycle in response to the westward deviation described
above, and most models including the skillful Google DeepMind keep
the center of Trudy offshore. However, note that small changes to a
track forecast that is parallel to the coast could result in large
differences regarding the severity of potential impacts. Users
should pay close attention to the watches and warnings in place and
continue monitoring forecast updates.
 
Additional strengthening is expected during the next day or so while
Trudy moves over very warm SSTs in a moist, low shear environment.
The near-term NHC intensity forecast lies on the high end of the
guidance (near HCCA) given the storm's current structure and these
favorable conditions. Southwesterly shear associated with a cutoff
low near northern Baja California is forecast to increase later this
weekend as Trudy moves northward, which could induce some weakening.
Potential land interaction further complicates the forecast, but
Trudy is predicted to remain offshore at this time and be a major
hurricane when it makes its closest approach to Mexico. Thereafter,
more significant weakening is forecast as the system encounters
even stronger shear and a drier mid-level environment.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to be a major hurricane when it approaches the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, bringing
an increasing risk of storm surge, damaging winds, and flooding
rain. Hurricane Watches and Tropical Storm Warnings are currently in
effect for portions of the coast, and additional watches and
warnings will likely be required today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest
coast of Mexico between Guerrero and Jalisco through the weekend.
This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides by
the weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacan,
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------

----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Simon was

rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3

please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.

item.title: Tropical Storm Simon Forecast Discussion Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 160840
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Simon Discussion Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Simon is gradually weakening. The storm continues to lose 
organization with intermittent bursts of deeper convection north of 
the center. A 0501 UTC Metop-C scatterometer pass showed a compact 
system with peak winds around 34 kt. Intensity estimates have 
dropped slightly, and the latest subjective Dvorak CI number from 
TAFB was 2.5/35 kt, but the Final T-number was 2.0/30 kt. Based on a 
compromise of these data, the initial intensity is lowered to 35 kt.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be northwesterly, or 310/08 kt. 
This general motion is forecast to continue through the weekend as 
the system moves in between a low-level trough to its west and a 
ridge to its east, bringing the weak and shallow system just west of 
the Baja California Peninsula over the weekend. The latest microwave 
and scatterometer data required a minor adjustment to the previous 
center position; therefore, the updated forecast track has been 
nudged northward accordingly, roughly between the corrected 
consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind (GDMI) ensemble.
 
Simon is anticipated to gradually weaken over the next 24–36 h due 
to an unfavorable environment of moderate to strong southwesterly 
vertical wind shear and dry mid-level air. As a result, Simon is 
expected to become a remnant low within 24 h and dissipate in about 
48 h.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
